paragraphs: At Levitt Chiropractic Center, we believe effective care starts with understanding the whole person, not just the symptoms. Led by Dr. Alan Levitt, who has been practicing chiropractic care since 1987, our clinic provides personalized, drug-free treatment designed to improve mobility, relieve discomfort, and support long-term wellness.

Whether you're experiencing chronic neck or back pain, recovering from a strain, or dealing with everyday stiffness and discomfort, our approach focuses on identifying the underlying factors contributing to your condition rather than simply addressing the symptoms.

We combine chiropractic adjustments with complementary therapies, including cold laser therapy, targeted exercises, and custom orthotics when appropriate. Every treatment plan is tailored to your individual needs, with an emphasis on restoring function and helping you feel your best.

Our whole-body philosophy considers how your posture, movement, lifestyle, and overall health influence your well-being. We take the time to listen, evaluate, and develop a thoughtful care plan that supports your health and quality of life.

items.q: What happens on a first visit?
items.a: You tell the real story — commute, desk, weekend miles, when it started. Then a hands-on exam. You leave knowing the next step. Imaging only when it would change care. No generic protocol.

items.q: Do you treat back pain without drugs or surgery?
items.a: Yes. Adjustments, cold laser, targeted ice, therapeutic exercise, and custom orthotics when the exam says they would change the load. The goal is the cause, not a pill that lasts until Thursday.

items.q: What is a red flag in chiropractic?
items.a: A red flag is a sign we should not just adjust: unexplained weight loss, night pain, fever, bowel or bladder changes, progressive weakness, or a significant recent trauma. Those need medical screening. A stiff neck after a week of commuting is a different story.

items.q: Can a chiropractor help heel spurs?
items.a: Often, yes — by calming the tissue around the spur and fixing the gait that keeps irritating it. Custom orthotics are sometimes part of that. We cannot sand a spur off the bone. If the pain is new, hot, and you cannot bear weight, we start with an exam, not a promise.

items.q: Can a chiropractor fix a wrist?
items.a: Many wrists, yes: joint restriction, repetitive strain, some carpal-tunnel patterns. Fractures, major ligament tears, and advanced arthritis need an orthopedic look first. We will say so if the exam is not a chiropractic case.

hero.title: Chiropractic Adjustments and Spinal Manipulation
hero.subtitle: Three techniques, chosen after the exam: Diversified, Zone Therapy, and Torque Release. Not a one-move routine.

intro.title: An adjustment is a decision, not a cracking sound
intro.beforeAddress: Dr. Alan G. Levitt, DC, chooses the contact after he has watched the joint move. He graduated from Northwestern College of Chiropractic in Bloomington in December 1986, has been in practice since 1987, and has worked at
intro.subluxation: A subluxation, in the language this site uses, is a spinal joint that is not moving well and may be irritating a nearby nerve. The adjustment is meant to restore motion at that joint. It is not described here as a cure for disease, and it is not sold as something you must hear pop. Some contacts are quick. Some are quiet. The sound is not the goal.
intro.methods: Other methods listed on the doctor’s biography, including applied kinesiology, Koren Specific Technique, Talsky Tonal Therapy, polarity, and muscle testing, are part of how he evaluates. They are not three extra adjustment brands. The three named techniques for the thrust or the regional work are below.

techniques.title: Which technique, and why that one
techniques.intro: You should be able to repeat the reason in your own words before you lie down.

items.title: Diversified
items.body: A quicker, direct contact. The office describes it as a thrust used to restore motion, ease tension, and improve how the joint lines up. It is not applied because it is the famous version. It is applied when the exam says that speed is appropriate.

items.title: Zone Therapy
items.body: Aimed at a region rather than one joint in isolation. The adjustment is paired with spinal massage so the area is treated as a connected set of parts, not an isolated click.

items.title: Torque Release
items.body: The gentler contact. The office describes it as a way to help the nervous system settle and communicate, without making a fast thrust the only option. It is the one we lean toward when a disc is irritable or a fast move is a poor fit.

who.title: Problems an adjustment may address
who.beforeNeck: Lower back pain, neck pain, headaches, other musculoskeletal pain, and subluxations. Each of those is explained with the condition it belongs to. Neck pain is
who.afterBack: The focus here is the contact itself.
who.headaches: Headaches are included only when the exam ties them to the neck or the upper back. A sudden severe headache, a headache after a head strike, or a headache with confusion is not an adjustment slot. Disc herniation is not “just adjusted.” If a nerve is weakening, disc care explains when we refer.
who.benefits: Benefits the office lists, and that we will not inflate, are less pain and tension for many mechanical problems, a change in how the joint moves, and a drug-free option before surgery is discussed. None of those is a promise for your case. Surgery and medication remain physician decisions.

visit.title: From paperwork to the contact
visit.arrival: Arrive 10 to 15 minutes early with a photo ID and clothes you can move in. The history is where it hurts, what changes it, and what has already been tried. The exam is hands-on. Imaging is selective. Then the technique is named. If today is not an adjustment day, you still leave with a reason.
visit.afterward: Afterward, soreness can happen. It is not required, and it is not proof the visit “worked.” Sharp new weakness, a headache that is unlike your usual one, or bowel or bladder change is a reason to call or to seek urgent care, not to wait for the next booked slot. Ordinary movement is usually encouraged unless a physician told you to rest.

skip.title: A red flag ends the adjustment conversation
skip.body: Major trauma that has not been cleared, progressive weakness, groin numbness, fever with spinal pain, unexplained weight loss, and pain that never changes with position are not “try a crack and see.” We screen and we refer. Keeping a visit on the book is not a clinical goal.

notice.title: What people notice in the hours afterward
paragraphs: Some joints feel easier to turn before you stand up. Some feel ordinary until the next morning. A mild ache in the muscles around the contact can show up and fade. That ache is not required, and it is not a score. A sharp line of pain into the arm or leg that was not there, new weakness, dizziness that does not settle, or a headache unlike your usual one is a reason to call the office or urgent care, depending on how severe it is.

The pop, if there is one, is gas shifting in a joint. Plenty of useful contacts are silent. Chasing the sound is how people get a technique they did not need. If you want Torque Release because you dislike the sound, say that. Comfort with the method is part of consent. It does not override a finding that says a fast contact is unsafe, and it does not mean a silent technique is weaker.

Follow-up is based on the retest. If rotation improved and stayed improved, the next visit may be further out, or it may be exercise only. If the neck locked again by dinner, the daily position is part of the problem and another thrust alone will not be the whole plan. We would rather lengthen the gap between visits when the exam allows than keep a standing weekly slot out of habit.

Children, older adults, and people with osteoporosis in their history get the same screening, not a louder version of Diversified. If a technique is a poor fit for bone density or for a fused area a surgeon created, it is not used there. Bring those records.             We will not discover a fusion by guessing.

If you have had spinal surgery, bring the levels that were fused or decompressed and the date. We do not adjust through a fusion and we do not argue with a surgeon’s restriction that is still in force. Adjacent segments can still be examined. That is a different sentence from “everything is adjustable.” People who want only the gentle option should say so at the start. People who want the visit over in two minutes should also say so. A rushed contact to honor a clock is not the technique list above. The visit takes the time the history takes.

items.q: What is a chiropractic adjustment?
items.a: A specific contact on a joint that is not moving the way it should. The neck after a long day and the low back after a week of sitting are the examples this office uses. You should know which technique and why before it happens.

items.q: Are adjustments safe?
items.a: They are a screened procedure, not a casual one. Dr. Levitt examines you first. A high-velocity contact is not the opening move after major trauma, unexplained weight loss, night pain that never changes, fever, or a change in bowel or bladder control. Those are medical problems until a physician says otherwise.

items.q: Will I be adjusted on the first visit?
items.a: Only if the exam says it is safe and useful that day. Some people leave the first visit with a plan and no thrust. X-rays are taken when they would change the plan, not as a routine. The first-visit steps are explained under what to expect.

items.q: How many adjustments will I need?

items.q: Do you only adjust the spine?
items.a: The techniques above are spinal and regional. They are used for low-back pain, neck pain, headaches, other musculoskeletal pain, and subluxations. Feet are a separate service when orthotics are the lever. Laser and ice are separate tools.

That is broader than we will claim. Digestion, allergies, and similar medical problems need the clinician who manages them. We can still look at the spine if you also have mechanical pain. We will not tell you the spine visit treated the other disease.

Some do not, and the useful response is to change the plan or the clinician. “Natural” is a description of the tools. It is not evidence, and it is not a timeline. line.title: Collaborate. Do not compete with your internist.
line.body: Most people who come here keep a primary clinician. That is the intended setup. If two offices are giving you opposite instructions about a drug or a surgery, ask them to talk, or pick the clinician whose license covers that decision. We will not quietly overrule a surgeon or a prescriber.

month.title: What a month of this approach can look like
paragraphs: Week one is the exam and, if it is safe, the first structural visit. You leave with one or two changes, not a new identity. Week two asks whether those changes were possible in a real schedule. If the exercise did not happen because it required a gym you do not have, the exercise was wrong. If the neck is worse, we do not congratulate you for “detoxing.” We retest.

Later weeks are allowed to get boring. Boring is a sign the plan fits. A plan that needs a new supplement, a new device, and a new explanation every visit is not more alternative. It is less accountable. We would rather repeat a small set that is changing the exam than refresh the menu.

Your physician’s month continues in parallel. Labs they ordered, drugs they manage, and referrals they made are not paused because you like the way a visit feels here. If our advice would collide with theirs, we stop and we sort it. Collision is a reason to talk, not a reason for you to pick the advice you prefer.

People sometimes ask for this kind of care because they are tired of being told to take something. Tired is understandable. It is not a diagnosis. If the exam is mechanical, we proceed. If the exam is not, we will disappoint you on purpose rather than invent a natural explanation for a medical problem.

Friends will offer remedies with more confidence than we will. A tea, a magnet, a cleanse, or a spine “reset” you saw in a video is not automatically part of care here because it is natural. If we do not use it, we will say we do not use it. You can still choose it on your own. You should not expect us to build the chart around it or to defend it to your physician. The work we will defend is the exam, the joint contact when it is indicated, and the small habit changes you agreed to try.

If you are comparing offices, compare the limits they will say out loud. An office that will not name a red flag, a referral, or a problem it does not treat is not more open-minded. It is less specific.             Specific is the standard on the rest of these service pages, and it is the standard here too. Bring the name of any approach you want us to react to. A clear “we don’t do that” is more useful than a vague nod. You will still get the exam. The exam is the part that does not depend on the label you arrived with.

items.q: How is this different from functional medicine?
items.a: Functional medicine is the wider history: sleep, food, and what you already take. Alternative medicine is the stance: try the non-operative, non-opioid options first when the exam supports them. Many visits use both ideas. They are not the same conversation twice.

items.q: Can this replace my medical treatment?
items.a: No. It can sit beside it. Do not stop a prescribed drug because you booked here. Emergency symptoms, cancer care, and mental-health crises stay with those clinicians.

items.q: Which complaints are a reasonable fit?
items.a: Mechanical pain in the neck, back, and joints, and people who want that pain approached without leading with medication or surgery. Headaches that the exam ties to the neck can be discussed. We do not promise results, and we do not treat the word “natural” as evidence.

hero.title: Back Pain Treatment, Including Sciatica
hero.subtitle: A mechanical exam for low-back pain and nerve pain down the leg. Drug-free care when the findings support it, and a referral when they do not.

intro.title: Most backs we see are mechanical. Some are not.
intro.mechanical: Back pain here is the ache from a desk, a lift, a long drive, or a weekend project, plus the leg pain that sometimes comes with it. Medication can take the edge off. Surgery has a place for a narrow set of nerve problems. Neither is the opening conversation for a joint or disc problem we can examine in Suite 201.
intro.sciatica: Sciatica is the name for irritation of the sciatic nerve. The nerve runs from the low back, through the buttock, and down the leg. When it is irritated, people feel pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness along that path. Bulging discs, a spinal joint that is not moving well, and muscle spasm can all increase pressure on it. Treating the word “sciatica” without finding which of those is involved does not help.
intro.beforeNeck: Both local back pain and sciatica, when the exam supports that label, are treated here. Neck pain is a different complaint. Neck pain that stays in the neck is covered under

patterns.title: Four ways back pain shows up
patterns.intro: These are descriptions, not diagnoses. Two of them can exist in the same person. The point of the list is to give you language for the history.

items.title: Local lumbar ache
items.body: Pain stays in the low back. Sitting, lifting, or standing up changes it. The leg feels normal.

items.title: Pain that travels
items.body: A line of pain, numbness, or tingling leaves the back and goes into the buttock, thigh, or calf. This is the pattern people call sciatica, and it still needs a cause.

items.title: Stiff, guarded back
items.body: The muscles lock after a lift, a long day at a desk, or a night of poor sleep. Motion is limited. The pain is broad rather than a thin line down one leg.

items.title: A back that keeps returning
items.body: The same spot flares every few weeks. Sometimes the driver is a joint that does not move well. Sometimes it is a disc, a hip, or the way the feet hit the ground.

sciatica.title: Leg pain needs a cause, not a stretch you found online
sciatica.pattern: A sciatica pattern is pain or sensory change along the nerve, often a line rather than a bruise. Coughing, sitting, or bending can make it louder. The ankle or big toe can feel weak. Those details tell the exam where to look. They do not diagnose you.
sciatica.sacroiliac: A common mix-up is the sacroiliac joint, where the base of the spine meets the pelvis. That joint can cause low-back pain and limit motion, and the symptoms overlap sciatica and a herniated disc. The joint can be tested in the exam. If that is the driver, the adjustment is aimed there, not at a disc that was never the problem.
sciatica.beforeOrthotics: A local muscle can ache in the buttock without being sciatica. Custom orthotics come up only when the way you stand keeps reloading the same side. They are prescription devices, not drugstore inserts. See the
sciatica.afterOrthotics: If the leg is getting weaker, use the red-flag list the same day.

Pain that wakes you and does not change no matter how you sit, stand, or lie

exam.physical: The physical exam checks motion, the joints that are not moving, nerve strength and sensation when the leg is involved, and whether the hip or the foot is feeding the problem. X-rays are taken when they would change the plan. An MRI is a physician-level decision when the nerve findings are concerning or conservative care is not the right next step. You should hear a working idea, what would change that idea, and which tools are actually on the table.

faqs.title: Questions about back pain and sciatica
faqs.intro: These are the questions that change what you do next. They are not outcome claims.

items.q: Is every pain down the leg sciatica?
items.a: No. Sciatica means the sciatic nerve is irritated, with pain, numbness, or weakness in the low back and the leg. A sacroiliac problem, a hip, or a local muscle can feel similar. The exam separates them.

items.q: Can a disc problem cause sciatica?
items.a: Yes. A bulging or herniated disc can irritate a nerve root, and so can a stiff joint or a muscle spasm. Which one you have is an exam question. Disc anatomy is part of degenerative disc disease care.

items.q: Do I need an MRI before the first visit?
items.a: Usually no. Imaging is recommended when it would change the plan. Bring films you already have. New weakness, groin numbness, or a bowel or bladder change should not wait on this appointment.

items.q: What treatments are actually used for back pain here?
items.a: Adjustments (Diversified, Zone Therapy, or Torque Release), cold laser, targeted ice, and therapeutic exercise, chosen from the exam. Custom orthotics are added only when the feet are part of the load. Medication and surgery stay with a physician when the findings call for them.

items.q: How long does back pain take to calm down?
items.a: There is no honest number before an exam. Some recent strains feel more mobile within a few visits. Long-standing patterns take longer, and some do not belong here. If the tests are not changing, the plan changes or you are referred.

items.q: Should I stop moving until the pain is gone?
items.a: Not for an ordinary mechanical backache, unless a physician told you to. Short walks and the exercises you are given usually beat a week on the couch. Stop a movement that sharply increases leg pain or weakness.

hero.title: Cold Laser Therapy
hero.subtitle: A handheld, low-level light used on the skin after an exam. No incision, no drug in the device, and no meaningful heat.

device.title: Cold laser therapy is light on the skin, for a short time
device.placement: Cold lasers at this office are handheld. Dr. Levitt places the unit directly over the area being treated. The time is 30 seconds to several minutes. The clock depends on how large the region is and on the dose that unit is set to deliver. You stay dressed except where the skin has to be reached. There is no incision.
device.cold: “Cold” means the beam is not trying to cut or to cook tissue. The practical difference is minimal temperature change: about 0.1 to 0.5 degrees Celsius if the skin warms at all. If you came in expecting a hot lamp or a surgical laser, this is a different tool. Cold laser therapy also does not put a medication through the skin.
device.beside: It sits beside the other care already offered here, not in front of the exam. Adjustments, targeted ice, exercise, and orthotics are separate decisions. Laser is added when the finding is something a light stimulus might reasonably calm, such as a stubborn tendon or a sore spinal region, and it is dropped when repeat checks show no change.

uses.title: Problems cold laser therapy may be considered for
uses.intro: The list is the one this office publishes. It is not a claim that light fixes each of them.
items: Acute and chronic pain
Ligament sprains and muscle strain
Soft-tissue strains
Tendonitis and tennis elbow
Arthritis and bursitis
Back pain
Carpal tunnel syndrome
Fibromyalgia
Wound healing, as an adjunct, not a substitute for medical wound care
uses.note: Back pain is a larger problem, because laser is only one piece of that plan. Carpal tunnel, tennis elbow, bursitis, and tendonitis are local tendon and joint problems the exam has to confirm. Arthritis here means the joint wear people already know they have, not a promise to rebuild cartilage. Fibromyalgia is a widespread pain problem without a single known cause on our conditions notes. Laser does not become the treatment for it by default. Wound healing, if it is discussed at all, is an adjunct. Open, infected, or surgical wounds belong with the clinician managing the wound.

visit.title: What actually happens in the room
visit.exam: The first appointment is still a history and a physical exam. Bring prior notes if another office has them. Dr. Levitt decides whether light belongs in the plan after that, not because you asked for cold laser therapy by name. X-rays are taken only when they would change the plan.
visit.room: If laser is used, you are positioned so the region is easy to reach. The device rests on or just over the skin. You should be able to say if anything feels sharp or too warm. Eye protection and aim matter: the beam is not pointed at the eyes. The visit can also include an adjustment or ice when those fit. It is not a gadget tour.

limits.title: What cold laser therapy will not do
limits.notDo: It will not close a fracture, drain an infection, or stand in for a surgeon when a nerve is failing. It will not reverse a herniated disc on an MRI. It is a poor substitute for the emergency department after major trauma. People sometimes hope a painless tool means a painless guarantee. The absence of a burn does not mean the underlying problem has to improve on a schedule.
limits.numbers: We also do not describe a biochemical pathway, a cell-energy number, or a success rate. Those figures are not in the office’s own description of the device. What is in the description is simple: light, short contact, little or no heat, no drug, no incision, used as one option among others.

limits.beforeIce: If the area is hot and swollen in the first days,
limits.afterIce: is the tool written for that, not laser. Neck pain, back pain, and disc problems have their own pages so this one can stay about the light.

expectations.title: Stop the light if the exam is standing still
expectations.body: Some people notice less guarding after a cluster of visits. Some notice nothing, which is useful information. We compare the same movements next time. A tendon that is unchanged after a fair trial does not get an open-ended laser schedule. Activity advice stays specific to the body part. There is no recovery date printed in advance.

cta.title: Ask if the light fits
cta.body: The exam comes first. Laser is added only when it matches the finding.

regions.title: The same light, different body regions
paragraphs: An elbow that hurts when you grip a coffee mug is a small target. The contact is short. The test next time is the grip, not a speech about cellular healing. A low back is a larger target, so the minutes run longer, and the test is sitting or bending, which back-pain care already explains. Laser does not become more “advanced” because the area is bigger.

Carpal tunnel symptoms need a neck and wrist screen before anyone aims a light at the wrist and calls it done. The median nerve’s story can start higher than the wrist. If the neck reproduces the hand symptoms, neck care is the better focus and laser on the wrist may be irrelevant. Tennis elbow that is actually a neck problem fails the same way.

Fibromyalgia is on the published list and is the easiest condition to overtreat with a device. Widespread pain does not mean widespread laser. If we use it, it is on a region that is disproportionately angry, and it stops when that region’s exam does not change. Wound healing stays an adjunct. A wound that is opening, draining, or was just closed in an operating room is managed by the clinician who owns the wound.

You can read, or you can talk, during the minutes the device is on. You should not be surprised by heat. If you are, we stop and we check the unit. Sessions are in the treatment room at the Saint Louis Park office, not a course you finish at home with a gadget bought online.

faqs.title: Questions about cold laser therapy
faqs.intro: The answers match the device this office actually uses.

items.q: What is cold laser therapy?
items.a: It is a low-level light treatment. The device is handheld, about the size of a flashlight, and the doctor holds it on the skin over the irritated area. A session on one region runs from 30 seconds to several minutes, depending on the area and the dose the unit delivers. It is not a heat lamp and not a surgical laser.

items.q: Does cold laser therapy hurt or burn?
items.a: It is non-invasive, with no incision and no drug in the device. The intensity raises tissue temperature only minimally, on the order of 0.1 to 0.5 degrees Celsius if the skin warms at all. Most people feel little or nothing while it is on. Tell us if the skin is uncomfortable.

items.q: Can I book cold laser therapy by itself?
items.a: It is one option inside a plan, after an exam. It is not a walk-in light treatment and it does not replace a history. If the exam says the problem is not something light can reasonably affect, we will not add it to fill the visit.

items.q: How many cold laser sessions are typical?
items.a: We do not quote a number before we see you. A recent strain and a long-standing tendon problem are not the same plan. If the findings are not changing, laser stops. There is no promise that a set of sessions will clear the pain.

items.q: Who should not start with laser?
items.a: Laser is not a clearance for a red-flag illness: unexplained weight loss, night pain that never changes, fever, a known cancer in the area being treated, or an eye problem under the beam. Those need a physician. We also do not aim the device at the eyes.

also.title: Other problems we are often asked about

items.title: Headaches
items.body: A headache that begins where the neck meets the skull can be mechanical, and that exam is part of neck care. Noise, fatigue, and stress can aggravate headaches without causing them. A sudden severe headache, a headache after a head strike, or a headache with confusion is an emergency. We do not quote a percentage of headaches that come from the neck.

items.title: Pinched nerve
items.body: The phrase means a nerve is irritated or compressed. In the neck that can show up in the arm. In the low back it can show up as sciatica. Neck care and back care sort those patterns. Weakness that is increasing is not a pinched-nerve wait.

items.title: Joint and sacroiliac pain
items.body: A stiff joint can hurt locally and can make the next joint work too hard. Sacroiliac pain, where the spine meets the pelvis, often imitates sciatica or a disc. It is tested in the back-pain exam, not diagnosed from a list. The adjustment, if one is used, is aimed at the joint the exam found.

items.title: Carpal tunnel and repetitive hand pain
items.body: Numbness, weakness, or burning with repetitive hand use can involve nerves that travel through the arm into the neck. Wrist pain still needs a screen for fracture and for a problem that belongs to a hand surgeon. An adjustment is not a carpal-tunnel cure. Laser is sometimes discussed for the soft tissue, and it has limits.

items.title: Osteoarthritis
items.body: Worn cartilage in a knee, hip, spine, or hand can hurt and can change how you move. Chiropractic care here can look at the motion you still have and at the compensation. It does not regrow cartilage. A hot, swollen joint with fever is medical, not a mobilization visit.

items.title: Fibromyalgia
items.body: Widespread pain without a single known cause, sometimes with poor sleep. We do not offer a cure. A visit can look for mechanical contributors and for sleep and load problems. It should not be presented as the treatment of the syndrome. Sleep and daily-habit questions, if they help, belong with functional medicine.

safety.title: Labels that should leave this list entirely
safety.flags: Chest pain, trouble breathing, a sudden severe headache, a blow to the head with vomiting or confusion, fever with spinal pain, progressive weakness, groin numbness, and a change in bowel or bladder control are not chiropractic conditions to browse. Use emergency care. Cancer treatment, infection, and a psychiatric crisis are not conditions we treat in this office.
safety.beforeBook: Maintenance visits are sometimes useful once a mechanical problem is understood. They are not a shield against those red flags, and they are not sold here as immune boosting or as guaranteed prevention you can count on. If you want a visit after the acute problem has settled, say that when you

cta.title: Not sure which problem?
cta.body: Book the exam and describe the symptom. We will sort the label.

describe.title: How to describe the problem when you call
paragraphs: Lead with place and behavior. “Left calf buzzes after twenty minutes of sitting, and the foot feels weak on stairs” is a back-pain problem until proven otherwise. “I cannot check a blind spot since Tuesday, no arm symptoms” is a neck-pain problem.

Mention what you have already tried only if it changed something. A week of a store-brand insert that did nothing is useful. A list of every video you watched is not. Bring the imaging report if a sentence on it scared you. The sentence is not the diagnosis until it matches the limb.

If you have two problems, say both, and say which one limits the day. You do not need the correct medical name before you are examined. Your appointment can cover more than one finding. It should not cover a medical emergency that you hoped would fit a chiropractic label.

We do not claim that spinal care treats allergies or the immune system. If that is what you were hoping to hear, you will not find that promise here. You will find an explanation that matches the pain, and a referral when the pain is not ours to treat.

Hand pain, jaw tightness, and rib pain sometimes get asked about in the same breath as the spine. A hand that is numb may still be a neck finding. Jaw pain and rib pain are worth mentioning even though they are not the main focus of care here. If they are outside what an exam can responsibly handle, you will be told before a plan is written, including when the next step is another clinician.

faqs.title: Questions about these conditions
faqs.intro: How we sort common problems, and which claims we do not make.

items.q: Do you treat every condition listed in one visit?
items.a: No. Neck pain, back pain and sciatica, and disc problems each have their own explanation below or in the links. Shorter notes here cover problems that are less often the whole story. The exam decides what is actually going on.

items.q: Do you still list allergies and similar conditions?
items.a: Allergy emergencies and immune disease belong with a physician. We do not claim spinal care treats the immune system. If you also have a mechanical spine problem, that part can be examined on its own.

items.q: Where do headaches go?
items.a: If they start in the neck, neck care is the right place to start. If the headache is sudden and severe, or follows a blow to the head, use emergency care and do not wait for a chiropractic slot.

items.q: Can one person have two of these at once?
items.a: Yes. A disc and a sacroiliac joint can both hurt, and a neck can be stiff while a back flares. The exam says which one is driving today. You do not need a separate philosophy for each label.

hero.subtitle: Targeted cold for hot, swollen, or freshly irritated tissue. Not a walk-in freeze chamber.

intro.title: Cryotherapy at this office means cold where it hurts
intro.chamber: Cryotherapy is often advertised as chambers, robes, and short exposures of the whole body. That is a different service. Levitt Chiropractic Center uses cold on the region that is hot, swollen, or freshly strained. The tool is an ice pack or a similar local application, applied in the visit and explained for home. A spa chamber is not what we offer.
intro.reasons: The practical reasons are straightforward: swelling and inflammation come down, acute pain is easier to tolerate, and the area can settle enough that other care is possible. It is drug-free. It is not a recovery promise. A numb patch of skin is a sensation, not proof that the problem is gone.
intro.afterPhone: . He has practiced since 1987 and at this office since 1999. Cold is one item he can add. It is not the identity of the practice.

timing.title: When cold earns a place in the plan
timing.intro: Four situations. If yours is not on the list, ask before you ice through a warning sign.

items.title: The first days after a strain
items.body: Tissue that is hot, puffy, or angry often gets cold before it gets anything else. That window is measured in days, not in a lifestyle.

items.title: A flare on an older problem
items.body: A back or neck that is usually mechanical can still have a hot day. Cold is for that day. It does not become the permanent plan.

items.title: After other work in the same visit
items.body: Ice is often used on the same visit as an adjustment or laser, on the region that was actually treated, not as a full-body finish.

items.title: When cold is the wrong idea
items.body: Poor circulation, numbness you cannot feel, broken skin, and a joint that looks infected are reasons to skip ice. We will say so.

alongside.title: Cold is rarely the only thing that happens
alongside.beforeAdjustments: An adjustment restores motion at a joint. Cold does not. On a day when the tissue is too irritable for a fast contact, ice may be the visit, and Torque Release or no thrust at all may be the judgment. Read
alongside.afterAdjustments: for the techniques. Do not expect cold to substitute for that decision.
alongside.beforeLaser: Cold laser therapy is light, not temperature. People mix them up because both are called “cold.” Laser does not chill the skin. Ice does. If you want the flashlight-sized device, that is the
alongside.afterLaser: . Booking cryotherapy when you meant laser wastes the first visit on vocabulary.
alongside.conditions: Back pain, neck pain, and a fresh sports strain can all be reasons to ice a region. The condition itself explains the problem. The explanation here is the cold itself. A fever with back pain, a joint that is red and you cannot bear weight, or pain after major trauma that has not been screened are not ice problems. Get medical care first.

home.title: The instructions matter more than the brand of pack
home.instructions: You will be told where it goes, how long, and what to put between the cold and the skin. The in-office range we use as a starting point is 15 to 20 minutes on the region. Longer is not braver. Sleeping on a pack is a common way to damage skin. If you cannot feel the area, do not ice it until someone who can see the skin has signed off.
home.beforeIce: The step-by-step home version is written on
home.beforeForm: Use that explanation for technique. Use the visit to decide whether cold belongs at all. Book through the
home.afterForm: if you have not been seen. There is no chamber fee and no pack price listed in advance.

limit.title: Cold buys calm. It does not finish the job.
limit.body: Swelling that is down tomorrow can be back if the load returns. That is not a failure of the pack. It is a sign the plan still needs the joint, the exercise, or a physician. We stop recommending ice when the area is no longer in that irritable window, even if icing has become a habit.

cta.title: Ask if cold fits today
cta.body: Tell us whether the area is newly hot or has been sore for months.

window.title: Cold is a window, then it should get smaller
paragraphs: On day one of a sprain, cold may be the main thing we do. On day four, if the puffiness is down and the joint will tolerate motion, cold becomes the thing you use after you overdo the walk, not the thing the visit is about. People who ice on a schedule forever have usually lost the plot. The plot was to calm the tissue so something else could happen.

Circulation is the contraindication people skip. If your hands or feet are already cold, pale, and poorly perfused, adding a pack because a teammate does it is a bad imitation. Raynaud-type color changes, a wound, and numbness from neuropathy are reasons we decline. You do not have to know the diagnosis. Describe the color and the feeling. We would rather skip cold than explain a skin damage later.

Same-day pairing is common and still selective. Ice after a contact that stirred a hot joint is reasonable. Ice on a neck that is only stiff from a pillow, with no heat and no swelling, may be unnecessary. Laser and cold are not a combo meal. If both are used, each one needs its own reason, said out loud.

Athletes sometimes ask for cold before they play. Numbing a joint so you can finish a game is not a service we provide. If you need the area numb to perform, you are not ready to perform. That conversation is more useful than a colder pack.

After the hot window closes, people still ask for cold because it is familiar. Familiar is not an indication. If the area is no longer swollen and the limit is stiffness, the next tool is usually movement, which is therapeutic exercise, or a joint contact, which is an adjustment. Keeping cold in the plan “just in case” fills time. We would rather end it.             You can always restart a pack for a new flare without making cold the identity of your care. If you are comparing this visit with a spa you saw advertised, compare the goal too. Theirs is often a whole body in a cold room for a few minutes. Ours is one region, long enough to calm it, then done. Those are not interchangeable appointments, and booking the wrong one helps neither of us.

faqs.title: Questions about cryotherapy
faqs.intro: Mostly to separate this office from a cryotherapy spa.

items.q: Is cryotherapy here a walk-in cold chamber?
items.a: No. Cryotherapy is often pictured as a spa chamber. This office uses targeted cold on the area that needs it. How to use the pack is covered with ice pack cryotherapy. We do not offer a whole-body chamber, and we do not quote a chamber temperature or a chamber session length.

items.q: How is this different from ice pack care?
items.a: This visit decides when cold belongs in a chiropractic plan, and when it does not. Ice pack care covers placement, time, and home use. Read both if you want the full picture. They are not two products.

items.q: How long is cold left on?
items.a: In-office cold on a region is described as usually 15 to 20 minutes. That is a guide, not a dare. Numb skin, a wrap that is too tight, or a pack straight on unprotected skin is how people get hurt. You leave with instructions that respect the skin.

items.q: Should I use heat instead?
items.a: Ice is generally the better first choice in the first 48 to 72 hours after a new strain or sprain, when the area is still irritable. After that, the choice depends on the exam. Heat on a hot, swollen joint is often the wrong experiment.

items.q: Will cold replace an adjustment or a doctor visit?
items.a: No. Cold turns down an angry area. It does not move a stuck joint, and it does not clear a fracture, a fever, or a nerve that is failing. Those still need the right exam.

fitting.title: What the appointment is actually for
fitting.shoes: Shoes come with you. The ones you work in matter more than the ones you wish you wore. We look at wear patterns, arches, and how the pelvis and spine sit on top of that. If a custom device is the right lever, it is prescribed. You should know what problem it is aimed at, and what it will not change.

after.body: The test is whether the pain they were built for is less provocative in the shoes you live in. If the back or heel is unchanged after a fair wear-in, we do not tell you to “give it a year” without looking again. Inserts also wear out. The “well over a year” line is the office’s general description, not a warranty printed here.

cta.body: We prescribe a pair only when the feet are part of the load.

weeks.title: The first two weeks in the pair
paragraphs: Day one is not an eight-hour test. Wear them for a portion of the day in the shoes that have enough depth, then come out of them if a new hot spot shows up. A hot spot is information about the shell or the shoe, not a character test. Call rather than layering moleskin for a month and deciding orthotics “failed.”

Look at the old insoles you removed. The wear pattern, heavier on one heel or one big toe, is part of why a custom shape was even considered. If both shoes are worn evenly and the pain is a disc with leg weakness, we should not have made the pair. That mismatch is on us to catch at the exam, which is why the shoes come to the visit before anything is ordered.

Running, a long shift on concrete, and dress shoes are three different loads. A pair that is comfortable in a sneaker can be miserable in a flat. We will say which shoes are realistic. We will not promise the pair works in every shoe you own, including the ones with no removable liner.

Recheck when the pain they were built for is either clearly better in those shoes or clearly not. “Well over a year” is how long the materials usually hold shape, not how long you should wait to complain. If the heel is worse, stop wearing them and come back.             Continuing to prove a point is how a helpful device becomes an irritant.

Socks, volume, and a shoe that was already tight are the boring reasons a good pair feels bad. If you add a thick sock on day three, the fit changes. Tell us that before we reshape anything. Children and people whose shoe size is still changing are a poor time to lock in an expensive shape. Say so if that is you. We would rather delay the pair than deliver something you outgrow before the break-in ends. None of this is a price. Ask the office what a pair costs for your case when you book. The number is not on the website.

items.q: What are custom foot orthotics?
items.a: Devices made for your feet that fit inside most shoes. They are shaped to your contours and to the way you walk, not pulled from a bin. A chiropractor can prescribe them. They are not the same object as a drugstore insert.

items.q: Will orthotics fix my back?
items.a: Only if the exam shows the feet are part of why the back, hip, knee, or neck keeps reloading. They ease pressure upstream when the stance is the lever. They do not fix a disc herniation, a hip that needs a surgeon, or a back problem that has nothing to do with gait.

items.q: Can orthotics help a heel spur?
items.a: The office’s position is narrow: we can often calm the tissue around a spur and the gait that keeps irritating it. We cannot sand a spur off the bone. A foot that is hot, red, or impossible to bear weight on needs a medical exam first.

items.q: Do they fit every shoe?
items.a: Most everyday and athletic shoes accept them. We look at the shoes you actually wear. A dress shoe with no depth may not. That conversation happens at fitting, not as a promise that every pair in the closet will work.

items.q: How long do they last, and what do they cost?
items.a: Most prescription orthotics last well over a year in regular use. We do not list a price here. Ask the office. Drugstore inserts are cheaper and often the wrong shape, which is a different problem from the sticker.

hero.title: Degenerative Disc Disease and Herniated Discs
hero.subtitle: What the disc finding means, which symptoms need a physician today, and how conservative care is chosen at this office.

disc.title: A disc is a spacer with a tough outside and a soft center
disc.spacer: Discs sit between the vertebrae. The outside is a tougher, rubbery layer. The center is softer. They allow the spine to move, keep space between the bones, and take load. Degenerative disc disease is not as much a disease as a name for the changes that show up as those discs age: less fluid, less height, less flexibility, and tears in the outer layer.
disc.changes: Those changes can lead to a herniated disc, a bulging disc, spinal stenosis, or osteoarthritis, or to nothing you can feel. Symptoms may sit at the disc or travel when a nerve is crowded, including numbness in an arm or a leg. The scan does not tell us which of those you are living with.
disc.beforeBack: Disc care here includes herniated disc care. Pain that stays in the low back or runs down the leg as sciatica is also covered, from the nerve-pattern side, on the

report.title: Degeneration, bulge, and herniation are not the same sentence
report.intro: Reports use these words loosely. Here is the distinction we use when we read one with you.

items.title: Degeneration
items.body: The disc loses fluid, gets shorter, and flexes less. Tears in the tougher outer layer are common with age. A scan can show this in a person who has no pain at all.

items.title: Bulge
items.body: The disc extends past its usual border in a broad way. It may crowd a nerve, or it may sit there without explaining the pain you feel today.

items.title: Herniation
items.body: Inner disc material pushes out through a weak spot in the outer layer. A herniated disc is more focal than a bulge. People also say slipped or ruptured. The words are not interchangeable, and the film has to be read with the exam.

items.title: Stenosis and joint wear
items.body: Degeneration can narrow the space around a nerve (spinal stenosis) or show up with osteoarthritis. Those are related findings, not a second disease you automatically have.

why.title: Age is the common factor. It is not the only one.
why.lead: Spines degenerate as a normal part of getting older. Other factors that show up in the history:
items: Aging, including outer-layer tears and loss of disc fluid
A specific event, such as a heavy lift or a fall
Repeated physical work
Smoking
Body weight that keeps a high load on the discs
why.after: A herniated disc after one lift or a fall is a different story from a disc that has dried out for years. Both can hurt, and both can be painless. Smoking and higher body weight are on the list because the office already names them as contributors, not as a lecture. Hot or cold packs and anti-inflammatory medication are common things people have already tried. Surgery is sometimes the right next conversation when nerve function is changing. Chiropractic care does not replace that conversation.

urgent.title: Disc pain with these signs is not a clinic appointment
items: Rapidly worsening weakness, or a new foot drop
Numbness in the groin, or a new change in bowel or bladder control
Fever, or pain that does not change with position
A recent hard fall or impact that has not been cleared by a physician
A surgery date that is already set for a progressive nerve problem
urgent.note: Those findings need a physician or an emergency department. Cauda equina symptoms, the groin and bowel or bladder group, are an emergency. Do not wait for a chiropractic opening.

film.title: The exam decides whether the herniated disc is the pain
film.bring: Bring the report and the images if you have them. The visit still starts with what you can do: walking, sitting, lifting your arm or your foot, and where the pain actually travels. A herniated disc on the left does not explain a right-leg problem. A degenerative label at a level that matches a dead nerve finding is a different visit from a degenerative label in a person who is stiff and strong.
film.beforeStreet: Dr. Levitt’s exam is the same standard as the rest of the practice. History, hands-on testing, and x-rays when they would change the plan. He has been in practice since 1987 and at
film.afterCity: since 1999. Technique choice, if an adjustment is appropriate, is among Diversified, Zone Therapy, and Torque Release, and it is biased toward the gentler option when a disc is irritable. You hear which one and why before it happens.
film.notSurgery: An adjustment is not surgical decompression, and it is not a promise to pull herniated material back into the disc. If someone offered you that outcome, it was not a description of this visit.

care.when: When the exam says it is safe, the plan uses services already on the site.
care.beforeAdjustments: An adjustment is a specific contact on a joint that is restricted. The aim is motion at that joint, which can reduce the guarding around a painful level. It is withheld when weakness is progressing or the history is a red flag. Read the
care.beforeLaser: Cold laser is a non-heat light held on the painful region for seconds to minutes, and it is dropped if it changes nothing. Targeted ice is for a hot flare. Exercise between visits is endurance, strength, and flexibility you can repeat at home. One stretch is not handed to every herniated disc. See
care.orthotics: Orthotics are uncommon for an isolated herniation. They come up when the feet keep reloading the spine. Your primary physician stays involved, and we do not stop medication they prescribed.

pace.title: Comfort can change before the MRI does
pace.scoreboard: The useful scoreboard is walking, sleep, and whether limb symptoms are shrinking, not a follow-up scan. Some people feel more capable over a series of visits. Some need a different clinician. We will not keep adjusting a worsening nerve to fill the schedule.
pace.activity: Activity inside a range that does not increase nerve pain is usually better than strict rest. A rounded, loaded lift is the habit most likely to flare a lumbar disc. “Never bend again” is not a plan.
pace.afterForm: if you want the exam. If you already have a surgical date for a progressive deficit, keep that date and bring the notes if you still want a second description of the conservative side.

cta.body: The exam compares the report with what your arm or leg can still do.

faqs.title: Questions about discs and herniations
faqs.intro: Short answers for the report you are holding. They are not a personal diagnosis.

items.q: Does degenerative disc disease mean my spine is diseased?
items.a: The name overstates it. It is the label for discs that have dried out and become less flexible with age. It is not an infection, and a scan can show it in someone with no pain. Pain depends on whether a nerve or a joint is actually irritated.

items.q: What is the difference between a herniated disc and a bulging disc?
items.a: A bulge is a broad extension of the disc. A herniation is inner material pushed through a more local weakness. Both can bother a nerve, and either can be an incidental finding. The distinction matters to a surgeon. It does not, by itself, pick the treatment.

items.q: Can chiropractic care help a herniated disc?
items.a: Sometimes, when the exam shows a mechanical problem that is safe to treat. Adjustments address joints that are not moving well. They do not push disc material back in, and they are not used when a nerve problem is worsening. Cold laser, ice, and exercise are the other tools here.

items.q: Should I be scared of an MRI that says herniated disc?
items.a: Bring the report. The useful question is whether the finding matches where you hurt and how strong the limb still is. Age-related disc changes are common. A new foot drop, groin numbness, or a bowel or bladder change is not a wait-and-see result.

items.q: Will the disc look normal again if I feel better?
items.a: Do not expect the MRI to rewind. The goal is pain, motion, and what you can do in a day. Some herniations become less dramatic. Many degenerative changes stay on the film. We will not promise either outcome.

items.q: When do you send someone to a surgeon?
items.a: When nerve function is getting worse, bowel or bladder control changes, conservative care is not changing a significant nerve finding, or a procedure is already scheduled for a reason we will not debate. We do not stop medication another physician prescribed.

intro.title: A wider history, not a second clinic
intro.whole: Functional medicine at Levitt Chiropractic Center is Dr. Alan Levitt’s whole-person visit. He still examines the spine. He also asks what else is going on when pain will not behave like a simple joint problem. The office describes that as looking at how the body is functioning, not only at the sore spot.

intro.root: “Root cause” is easy to overread. Here it means we try not to chase a single symptom with a single trick. It does not mean we have found a hidden diagnosis the rest of medicine missed. If the history sounds medical, you keep your physician, and we say so.

items.body: Musculoskeletal pain can sit next to poor sleep, a limited diet, or a day with no real movement. The visit writes those down. It does not assume they are the cause.

items.body: Adjustments are still available when a joint is not moving. Functional medicine does not retire the structural visit. It adds questions when the history says the pain is not only a joint.

examples.title: Where a wider plan shows up in real complaints
examples.beforeBack: Back pain that returns every Sunday night may be a joint, and it may also be a chair and a sleep position. The
examples.afterBack: visit owns the mechanical sort. This visit adds the week around it when the mechanical sort is not the whole story.
examples.beforeNeck: Headaches are another example already on the site: stress, diet, movement, and manipulation can all be discussed. That is not a migraine program, and a sudden severe headache is an emergency. Neck pain itself is on the
examples.fibromyalgia: Fibromyalgia, as the conditions notes say, has no single known cause and no cure we can offer. A visit can still look for contributors to the pain and for sleep trouble. It should not be sold as the answer to the syndrome. Sciatica and disc disease stay on their own pages; functional questions are extra, not a replacement exam.
examples.nutrition: Nutrition advice here is ordinary and specific: what you eat, what you skip, and whether a supplement you already bought is doing anything you can notice. We do not publish calorie targets or sell a detox. If you need a dietitian or a medical workup for weight, blood sugar, or gut disease, that referral is part of an honest plan.

boundaries.title: What this visit refuses to be
boundaries.beforeAlternative: It is not anti-medicine. Alternative medicine uses that same line: non-surgical and non-opioid first, not opposed to physicians. Read
boundaries.afterAlternative: if you want the drug-free framing. Stay here if you want the habit and nutrition questions spelled out.
boundaries.guarantee: It is not a guarantee of lasting results. Older marketing on Some descriptions promise benefits for years or decades. That is a hope, not a finding we can promise. Chronic problems often change slowly, and some do not change with this kind of care.
boundaries.beforeAddress: Bring a photo ID, a medication list, and a rough picture of sleep and meals. The address is
boundaries.afterBooking: . Dr. Levitt has practiced since 1987 and at this office since 1999.

afterward.title: The plan should fit a week you actually have
afterward.body: You should leave knowing which part is structural, which part is a habit, and which part needs another clinician. Two changes you can keep are better than a binder. If nothing in the exam or the habits is moving after a fair trial, we stop pretending the next month will be different and we refer.

cta.title: Start with the wider history
cta.body: Bring your medication list. We will not take you off anything a physician prescribed.

notes.title: A week of notes that is actually usable
paragraphs: If sleep is part of the story, write down the hour you get in bed and the hour you give up, for a few nights. Do not produce a perfect diary. A pattern of waking at 3 a.m. with a stiff back is different from a pattern of never getting horizontal before midnight. Those two nights suggest different next steps, and neither one is a supplement.

Food notes can be equally plain. What you ate on the day the pain spiked, and whether you skipped meals, is enough to start. We are not scoring macros. A person who is dizzy because they do not eat before a morning visit does not need a protocol. They need breakfast and a clearer exam. Gut disease, unexplained weight change, and blood in the stool are physician problems we will name as such.

Movement notes belong here too, but the exercises themselves are written with the exercises so this visit does not become a workout sheet. “I sit nine hours and walk to the printer” is a functional finding. The response might be a walking break. It might be a chair change. It might be irrelevant if the exam shows a disc with a true nerve deficit. The wider history loses when it competes with a dangerous finding.

Bring the bottles you already own if you want them looked at. We will not add a stack of new ones to look thorough. If a product is interacting with a prescription, that question goes back to the prescriber.             Our role is not to referee the pharmacy.

Bring a short list of questions you actually want answered, not a printout of a forum thread. “Should I change breakfast, or is the back the whole story?” is a usable question. “Can you balance my hormones?” is not a service we advertise, and we will not pretend a spinal visit does that. If the honest answer is a referral to primary care, you should hear it in the first visit rather than after a month of vague advice. Write down what we agreed to try and what we agreed not to touch. That note is the plan.

faqs.title: Questions about functional medicine
faqs.intro: Plain answers about what this office does and does not add to chiropractic care.

items.q: How is functional medicine different from an adjustment?
items.a: An adjustment is a contact on a joint. Functional medicine, as this office describes it, looks at the wider picture: sleep, nutrition, habits, and how those sit next to the pain. You can have both in one plan. You do not have to pick a philosophy.

items.q: Will I have lab work or genetic testing?
items.a: We do not offer a lab menu or a genetic test. The history can run from what you already know about your health to daily habits. If a test would help, that order belongs with the physician who runs it. We will not invent a panel to justify the visit.

items.q: Do I stop my medication?
items.a: No. Functional medicine here is complementary. Do not change a prescription because of a chiropractic visit. Your prescribing clinician stays in charge of those drugs.

items.q: Which problems does the office connect to this visit?
items.a: We already connect fibromyalgia, sciatica, joint pain, and degenerative disc disease as examples where a wider plan is sometimes useful. Each of those still needs its own exam. Sciatica and disc findings are examined for what they are. This visit does not replace that exam.

items.q: Is this a cure for chronic illness?
items.a: No. The office talks about looking for contributors and about habits that can be changed. It does not promise years or decades of relief, and it does not claim to cure a medical disease. If the story sounds like infection, cancer, or a psychiatric crisis, that is not this appointment.

hero.title: Ice Pack Cryotherapy
hero.subtitle: How a cold pack is used on a fresh strain or sprain: a barrier, a small area, and a timer. Not a full-body freeze.

intro.title: Ice is a local compress with rules
intro.effects: An ice pack in this office is a cold compress on a fresh or flared spot. The effects we rely on are narrower than advertising: muscle spasm can ease, sensation in the irritated spot drops while the cold is on, soft tissue cools, and inflammatory soreness is often quieter. Those are temporary effects. They are useful. They are not a repair.
intro.intent: Rehabilitation programs and chronic-pain days both show up in the old description. The difference is intent. After a new sprain, ice is there to get you through the hot window. In a longer problem, ice is for the flare, then the actual plan (joint, exercise, or a referral) has to exist. Icing the same spot every evening for a year is not a treatment plan.
intro.afterPhone: . Dr. Levitt decides whether you even need the pack. The steps below are what we mean by using one safely.

steps.title: A pack you can repeat without guessing
steps.intro: This is the home version of what the visit demonstrates.

items.title: Skin check
items.body: Look at the area. Skip the pack over open skin, a rash that might be infection, or skin you cannot feel.

items.title: A layer
items.body: Do not put a bare frozen pack on skin. A thin cloth is the usual barrier. The goal is cooling, not a burn from cold.

items.title: The region only
items.body: The pack covers the part that is hot or freshly strained. It is not wrapped around the whole limb for sport.

items.title: A short timer
items.body: Start from the office guide of about 15 to 20 minutes. Set a timer. Do not fall asleep on it.

items.title: Recheck
items.body: Skin should look pink and recover, not stay white, blistered, or numb for a long time. Stop and call if it does.

where.title: Sprains, post-visit soreness, and the weekend overdo
where.situations: A sprained joint, soreness after an adjustment, and the first two or three days after you lifted something cold are the situations the office names. The pack goes on the region, often in the same visit as other care, and you leave knowing the home version. It is not applied over a numb neuropathy, and it is not a treatment for a foot you cannot stand on until that foot has been medically seen.
where.beforeNeck: Neck and back flares can be iced if the exam says the tissue is the irritable part. The neck problem itself is explained on
where.athletes: Athletes sometimes want ice as a ritual. A ritual is fine if the skin rules hold. It does not shorten a ligament’s calendar.

mistakes.title: The ways a pack causes a new problem
mistakes.errors: Direct frozen plastic on skin, an hour instead of twenty minutes, a pack under a sleeping person, and ice over a patch you cannot feel are the errors. Chemical packs that leak are another. If the product says not to apply it to skin, believe the product. We are not describing a brand.
mistakes.beforeExercise: Heat-versus-ice arguments online are louder than the decision deserves. Irritable and swollen leans cold, especially in the first 48 to 72 hours. Stiff and calm can lean toward gentle movement, which is
mistakes.afterExercise: , not a heating pad marathon. When you are unsure, call before you invent a routine.
mistakes.beforeCryo: if no one has looked at the problem. Why we choose cold, rather than a spa chamber, is explained with

better.title: Quieter tissue, then a real next step
better.body: A useful pack makes the next few hours more tolerable and keeps the swelling from running the day. It does not have to erase the problem. If you need the pack more, not less, after several days, the area needs another look. That look might be here. It might be urgent care. The trend tells us which.

cta.title: Have the area looked at
cta.body: We will show you placement and time if cold is actually the right tool.

placement.title: Where the pack sits, by body part
paragraphs: An ankle that rolled gets the pack over the swollen side, not wrapped so tightly the toes go white. You should still see the toes. A shoulder that is hot after a fall gets the pack on the sore face of the joint while the arm is supported, not dangling. A low back after a lift gets a pack across the painful band while you are lying down, so you are not leaning on the ice.

A neck is awkward. The pack has to stay put without a strap that chokes, and you should not lie on it. If you cannot arrange that safely, do not improvise with a scarf pulled tight. Come in and we will show you, or skip home ice until you can. Neck pain care still covers the cause. The pack is only the compress.

After an adjustment, some people want ice out of habit. Use it if the area feels hot or guarded. Skip it if you feel ordinary. Soreness that is just muscle effort often prefers a short walk over another twenty minutes of cold. Therapeutic exercise is where that walk gets specific.

Frozen peas are a pack if they are in a cloth and you do not eat them afterward once they have thawed and refrozen badly. A dedicated gel pack is fine if it stays intact. Leaking gel on skin is a chemical problem, not a chiropractic one. Rinse and get medical help if the skin reacts.             We are not endorsing a brand, a temperature, or a freezer setting.

A pack that was used on broken skin, or that smells like solvent, is done. Throw it out. Do not rinse and reuse a leaking chemical pack. If you share a household freezer, label the pack so nobody treats it as food. That is the entire hygiene talk. The clinical talk is still whether the problem needs a person to look at it. Ice you already did at home does not replace that look, and it does not count as having “tried chiropractic.”

faqs.title: Questions about using an ice pack
faqs.intro: Skin, timing, and when to stop. Not a product recommendation.

items.q: How do I ice at home without damaging skin?
items.a: Use a cloth between the pack and the skin, cover only the region you were shown, and keep it near 15 to 20 minutes. Set a timer. If the skin stays pale, blisters, or you cannot feel it, stop. Numbness is a reason to quit, not a sign to continue.

items.q: How often can I repeat it?
items.a: During a hot, new flare, several times in a day is common, with the skin back to normal between rounds. The office will give you the rhythm for your case. More hours of ice are not a stronger treatment.

items.q: Ice or heat after the first few days?
items.a: The first 48 to 72 hours after a new strain or sprain usually favor ice if the area is still puffy and irritable. Later, the exam decides. Heat can feel good on a stiff, non-swollen muscle and can annoy a joint that is still hot. Do not switch because a forum said to.

items.q: Is an ice pack the same visit as cryotherapy?
items.a: Same cold, two explanations. Cryotherapy explains when this office uses cold instead of a spa chamber. Ice pack care is where the pack sits, how long, and what your skin should do. You do not book them as two different products.

items.q: Can I ice a neck or back before I have been examined?
items.a: A brief, protected pack on a simple strain is a reasonable home step while you arrange a visit. Do not ice through a red flag: fever, pain after major trauma that has not been checked, progressive weakness, or a change in bowel or bladder control. Those are not pack problems.

hero.title: Neck Pain, Pinched Nerves, and Desk-Related Stiffness
hero.subtitle: An exam for pain that stays in the neck, travels into the arm, or shows up as a headache from the base of the skull.

intro.title: Understanding neck pain
intro.beforeAddress: Neck pain at Levitt Chiropractic Center may stay in the neck, travel into the arm, or begin as a headache at the base of the skull. Dr. Alan Levitt has been in practice since 1987 and at
intro.beforeBack: People arrive with a neck that locked after sleeping, a shoulder that burns by the end of a screen day, or an arm that tingles when they turn. Those are different stories. Low-back pain and sciatica are treated as
intro.nerve: A pinched nerve means something is irritating a nerve: a joint that will not move, a disc that has changed shape, or a muscle in spasm. Pressure can bring inflammation, pain, and sometimes weakness. The visit is for finding which of those fits. The name alone does not identify the structure.

patterns.title: How neck pain can feel
patterns.intro: Use these as history, not as a diagnosis you give yourself.

items.title: A stiff local neck
items.body: Turning to check a blind spot or looking up is limited. The pain stays in the neck or the top of the shoulder. The arm feels normal.

items.title: Pain or tingling into the arm
items.body: A line of pain, numbness, or weakness leaves the neck and travels into the shoulder blade, arm, or hand. That pattern needs a nerve check, not a guess.

items.title: Headache that starts at the skull base
items.body: Some headaches begin where the neck meets the skull and move toward the temple or behind the eye. Other headaches do not come from the neck at all.

items.title: The screen-day neck
items.body: Patients call the ache after a day of looking down “tech neck” or “desk neck.” It is a description of the posture, not a separate disease.

desk.title: Neck pain from desk work and sleep
desk.head: The head is heavy when it sits forward of the shoulders. A long meeting, a phone in the lap, or a pillow that keeps the neck kinked can leave the joints stiff and the muscles guarding. People call that tech neck. What we can check is whether the joints actually move, whether the arm is strong, and whether the headache, if there is one, starts in the neck.
desk.headache: A headache from the neck often begins at the skull base. Noise, fatigue, and stress can make any headache louder, but they do not prove the cause. We do not use a percentage for how many headaches come from the neck. If the exam points at the neck, care is aimed there. If it points somewhere else, we say so.
desk.sleep: Sleep position matters in the history. So does the work setup, in plain language: screen height, how long you sit, and what you do on breaks. We will not hand you a gadget list. Two or three changes you can keep beat a perfect desk you abandon.

urgent.title: See a physician or the ER before an adjustment
items: Neck pain after a fall, trauma, or hit to the head that has not been medically screened
Progressive arm or hand weakness, or new trouble walking or using the hands
A sudden severe headache, confusion, fainting, or repeated vomiting
Fever with severe neck pain, or pain that never changes with position
Bowel or bladder change, which is uncommon in an ordinary stiff neck and is an emergency

visit.title: What the neck exam is looking for
visit.paperwork: Bring a photo ID and plan on 10 to 15 minutes of paperwork. Tell us when it started, whether the arm is involved, and what a turn or a cough does to it. Prior imaging and any medication another clinician prescribed belong in that history.
visit.beforeExpect: Dr. Levitt checks motion, the joints that are stuck, and strength and sensation when the arm is part of the story. X-rays are taken when they would change the plan, which is the same rule as the rest of the practice. You should leave with a working idea and the next step. The first-visit outline is on
visit.beforeAdjustments: If an adjustment is appropriate, the technique is Diversified, Zone Therapy, or Torque Release. Diversified is a quicker contact. Torque Release is gentler. Zone Therapy includes spinal massage for the region. You hear which one before it happens. More on technique is under
visit.afterAdjustments: A fast thrust is not the opening move after unexplained trauma or when arm strength is falling off.

added.title: Other care that may be included
added.beforeLaser: Cold laser therapy is a handheld light, about the size of a flashlight, held on the sore area for 30 seconds to several minutes. It does not heat the skin in any meaningful way. It is optional and it is dropped if the neck exam is not changing. Learn how
added.afterLaser: is used before you ask for laser alone.
added.beforeExercise: Targeted ice is for a neck that is hot and newly irritated. It is not a whole-body cold chamber. A few exercises for endurance, strength, or mobility are how a neck stays looser between visits.
added.afterExercise: covers endurance, strength, and mobility. A long stretch sheet you will not do is not the plan.
added.beforeDisc: A disc in the neck may be degeneration, a bulge, or a herniation.
added.afterDisc: explains those findings against the arm exam. An adjustment is not a promise to put disc material back. If hand clumsiness or walking is getting worse, that is a physician visit.
added.beforePhone: Ordinary activity that does not spike arm pain is usually better than a week of holding the neck perfectly still. We will not promise a visit count. Call

recovery.title: What improvement can look like
recovery.body: The scoreboard is turning your head, sleeping, and whether the arm symptoms are shrinking. Some recent necks feel more movable after care starts. A neck that has guarded for a long time needs the daily position changed as well. If strength is dropping, we stop and refer. Feeling better is the hope. It is not a guarantee, and we do not quote a fee before the exam.

cta.body: Tell us if the pain stays local, travels down an arm, or becomes a headache.

faqs.title: Questions about neck pain
faqs.intro: These answers are for booking and for sorting emergencies. They are not a personal diagnosis.

items.q: What is a pinched nerve in the neck?
items.a: It means a nerve is irritated or compressed. A stiff joint, a disc bulge, or muscle spasm can do that. The result can be pain, tingling, or weakness in the arm. The name does not tell us which structure is involved until the exam.

items.q: Can a headache come from the neck?
items.a: Sometimes. A headache that starts at the base of the skull can be mechanical. Migraines, sinus pain, and a sudden severe headache are different problems. A headache with confusion, a blow to the head, or the worst pain of your life needs emergency care, not an adjustment.

items.q: Which treatments does this office use for the neck?
items.a: After the exam, the options already offered here are spinal adjustments (Diversified, Zone Therapy, or Torque Release), cold laser, targeted ice, and a few home exercises. The gentler contact is chosen when a fast thrust is a poor fit. Surgery, injections, and prescription drugs are not services of this office.

items.q: How many visits will a stiff neck take?
items.a: There is no number before the exam. Some recent mechanical necks loosen over a short series. A neck that has been guarded for months, or an arm that is weak, is a different plan. If the same tests are not changing, the plan changes or you are referred.
