hero.title: Therapeutic Exercise
hero.subtitle: A few specific movements for endurance, strength, or flexibility. Built for the problem we found, and for a week you will actually do.

homework.title: Exercise here is a prescription, not a personality
homework.pain: The pain that eases on the table and returns on Thursday is often a strength and habit problem sitting next to the joint. Therapeutic exercise is how this office asks those muscles to work. It is not a boot camp, and it is not a stack of pages. The office’s own line is endurance, resistance, and flexibility, chosen for you.
homework.afterPhone: , since 1999 at this address and since 1987 in practice. He will not hand you another person’s packet. If you already have exercises from a physical therapist or a surgeon, bring them. We do not casually overwrite a post-surgical restriction.

kinds.title: Endurance, resistance, flexibility
kinds.intro: Most plans use one or two of these, not a sampler of all three on day one.

items.title: Endurance
items.body: Repeating a tolerable movement long enough that the neck or back can last a workday. This is stamina of the part that failed, not a running program you did not ask for.

items.title: Resistance
items.body: Load, progressed slowly, so the muscles that should have protected the joint actually can. Body weight is enough for most of what we send home. A gym is not required.

items.title: Flexibility
items.body: Range you lost to guarding. The stretch is specific. A generic hamstring poster is not automatically your exercise, and forcing a painful direction is not flexibility.

aims.title: Aims already listed by the office
items: More usable motion
Less unnecessary tension in muscle and the tissue around it
Joints that move instead of hitching
Circulation during the movement, not as a slogan
Balance and coordination when those were part of the problem
Less rigidity in a back or neck that has been braced for weeks
aims.breathing: Breathing and coordination are on that list because some people brace so hard they stop moving well. We are not running a breathing seminar. If balance is unsafe, the exercise is paused. Dizziness, a truly unstable inflammatory flare, and the period after some surgeries are reasons to wait. The wait is a medical decision, not a motivational one.
aims.beforeDisc: Neck exercises are not low-back exercises. A disc that prefers one direction does not get the opposite stretch because it was on a poster. The
aims.afterDisc: says that directly. Neck ownership is

program.title: Shown in the room, then cut down until it fits
program.shown: You do the movement once with feedback. If the form falls apart, the exercise is too ambitious and it gets simpler. You leave with a number of repetitions you can remember. Writing “3 sets of 15” for twelve moves is how sheets die in the car. We would rather you own two.
program.beforeIce: Soreness the next day can be ordinary effort. Pain that changes where it travels is not. Ice after a session is optional and is optional, as with an
program.beforeAdjustments: , for flares, not as a required chaser. An adjustment can still be the visit when the joint, not the muscle, is the limit. See
program.beforePhone: There is no class schedule and no fee chart here. Call
program.beforeAddress: . Wear clothes you can move in. The address is

progress.title: The exercise worked if the week got easier
progress.body: We recheck the same task: longer sitting, an easier lift, a turn of the head that no longer pinches. A perfect workout log with the same pain is not progress. If the movements are honest and the pain is not changing, the plan changes. That can mean a different exercise, a different service, or a different clinician. It does not mean “try harder.”

cta.title: Get a short list, not a packet
cta.body: We match endurance, strength, or mobility to the exam.

examples.title: Examples of a short list, not a program to copy
paragraphs: A neck that stiffens at a laptop might get two drills: a slow turn each direction that stays short of arm pain, and a shoulder-blade squeeze you can do in a chair. Those are illustrations of size, not a prescription you should start from this paragraph. Your list is written after the neck exam.

A low back that hates long sitting might get a short walk on the hour and a hip hinge practiced with a broomstick so the spine does not round under a box. Again, an illustration. If sitting is fine and lifting is the trigger, the list flips. Sciatica that worsens with one of those moves gets that move deleted the same day.

An ankle sprain, once a clinician has said it is not a fracture, might later get balance on one foot beside a counter. Early on, the homework may only be protected range, not balance. Healing sets that timing. The homework still has to match the stage.

People ask for “core” work. If the abdomen is bracing so hard the back cannot move, more bracing is the wrong hobby. If the back collapses the moment you pick up a bag, some endurance in the trunk may be the missing piece. The word core is not specific enough to be the plan.

Write the list where you will see it. A note on the phone beats a PDF. Recheck in the office by doing the move, not by saying you did it.             If two weeks of honest practice leave the same limitation, we change the move or we stop calling exercise the answer.

Travel weeks, night shifts, and childcare change the dose. Say which week you are actually in. A plan that assumes a quiet morning on the floor will be skipped, and then both of us will pretend it failed. Five minutes beside the counter can be the honest version. Holding your breath and racing the reps is not endurance. It is rushing. Slow enough to keep the form is the point of a short list. If you need a video to remember, we can describe the move in words you can film yourself doing once in the room, for you, not for the internet.

Stop entirely if you are ill, if a surgeon has not cleared a recent operation, or if the pain has changed sides or started traveling. Restart only after someone looks again. Consistency is useful. Consistency through a new nerve symptom is not discipline. It is the wrong assignment. If you miss several days, resume at the easier dose rather than doubling up to catch up. Catching up is how a tolerable move becomes a flare. Tell us what you actually did. The retest is more honest when that report is.

faqs.title: Questions about the home exercises
faqs.intro: Equipment, pain rules, and what this is not.

items.q: Do I need a gym membership?
items.a: No. Most of what Dr. Levitt prescribes can be done at home with little or no equipment. If a movement needs a band or a light weight, that is said out loud. A membership is not the treatment.

items.q: How often are the exercises done?
items.a: Often several days a week, matched to the week you have, not to an ideal athlete’s calendar. A short session you complete beats a long sheet you avoid. We change the dose if soreness is replacing the movement.

items.q: Will exercise replace the adjustment?
items.a: Not when a joint is stuck and needs a contact. Exercise is how the gain survives until the next visit, and sometimes how you need fewer visits. The adjustment is the contact. The homework is what you repeat at home.

items.q: What if the exercise increases pain?
items.a: Stop that one and tell the office. Muscle effort can feel unfamiliar. Sharp pain, pain that travels farther down an arm or leg, or new weakness is not effort. Do not push through a nerve symptom.

items.q: Is this physical therapy?
items.a: It is therapeutic exercise prescribed inside this chiropractic office: endurance, resistance, and flexibility aimed at the problem we found. It is not a physical therapy clinic, and it is not a post-surgical protocol unless the surgeon has cleared you to move.

items.q: Is chiropractic effective?
a: Chiropractic helps to remove postural imbalances and structural misalignments that can accumulate in our bodies over time. Chiropractic works by restoring your own inborn ability to be healthy.

For your body to remain healthy, your nervous system must function well. For your nervous system to function well it must be free of interference. By restoring spinal function with chiropractic adjustments, nerve interference by misaligned vertebrae is removed thus allowing optimal nervous system function and improved health.

items.q: Why should I see a chiropractor?
a: Seeing a chiropractor is not only for back pain and neck pain. Chiropractic care is an excellent way to keep your body at its peak performance through nutrition, adjustment, and overall wellness.
In addition, chiropractic care has been known to help a wide range of conditions from fibromyalgia to diabetes.

items.q: What is subluxation?
a: When a vertebra becomes misaligned or moves out of its normal position, this is referred to in the chiropractic profession as a subluxation. Subluxations can be caused by a wide range of issues from a minor slip or bump to any sudden trauma.

When a vertebra is subluxated, it begins to put pressure on nerves, blood vessels, and everything around it. This pressure comes with a price: the subluxation interrupts the natural pathways that messages from the brain need to be clear in order to be completed properly.

items.q: How does chiropractic care work?
a: Chiropractic is an overall way of looking at the human body. It’s based on the idea that the body is self-sustaining and self-healing. The body is essentially controlled by the brain through its connection via the spinal cord and the vast networks of nerves that make up the body.

In the chiropractic world, drugs and medicine are not utilized as a form of treating a patient. While supplementation and nutrition are almost always a part of the bigger picture, drugs and prescriptions can be viewed as band-aids to treat symptoms rather than going to the source.

Chiropractors not only treat soft and hard tissue problems such as sciatica and joint pain, but are largely called on to deal with more significant issues fibromyalgia, allergies, insomnia, headaches, and many more.

items.q: What is a chiropractic adjustment? Is it safe?
a: Adjustments, or manipulation as they’re sometimes referred to, is the minor movement of vertebrae in the spine. The objective of this movement is to realign vertebrae that have moved out of place for a number of reasons from normal daily activity to sudden trauma.

When these vertebrae are out of place, it has an overall systemic effect from muscular to the central nervous system. Without proper alignment and flow of all nerves and systems in the body from the brain, we can’t function at our peak.

An adjustment is often pressure from the chiropractor utilizing the hands or an instrument to move a vertebra back into place. This happens with a quick movement and is often without discomfort. You may hear a noise that sounds like cracking your knuckles joint cavitation which is the release of gases such as oxygen and nitrogen from the joint.

items.q: What can I expect from my visit to a chiropractor?
a: Going to the chiropractor is a new experience for many of us. Maybe we’ve heard through a friend or have done some research online. It’s possible that you are just fed up with living in pain and it’s time to do something about it.
In either case, your first visit to the chiropractor will really be about getting to know the chiropractor and discussing your history, current condition, and goals.

items.q: What results can I expect from treatment?
a: Chiropractic is based on the idea of removing imbalances both structural and postural in an effort to allow our body to heal itself. For this to happen, the network of nerves and signals from your brain down your spinal cord, to the network of nerves must be allowed to flow freely without any interruption.
Chiropractors have the ability and skill to remove these interruptions or misalignments and allow the body to perform as it was meant to.

If you’ve ever experienced a fall, repetitive strain, or just bumped into something too hard, it’s very possible that you are not functioning at your best due to a misalignment. While there are many potential mechanical or structural causes for misalignment, there are also chemical reasons smoking, drinking excessively, or even just a poor diet can cause underlying conditions and disease to appear.
Allowing a chiropractor to get you back on track both chemically and structurally will bring your body back to the proper state it should be in to perform at its peak.

hero.title: Spinal Wellness Tips
hero.subtitle: Small daily habits posture, lifting, sleep, movement that protect your spine and keep you feeling your best.

intro.title: Small habits, big payoff
intro.body: The way you sit, sleep, lift, and move shapes the health of your spine more than any single adjustment. These are the habits we recommend most often to our patients easy to start, hard to regret.

items.title: Sit smarter at your desk
items.body: Keep your feet flat on the floor, hips slightly higher than knees, and the top of your screen at eye level. Stand or stretch every 30–45 minutes your spine is not designed for all-day sitting.

items.title: Lift with your legs
items.body: Squat down to the load, keep it close to your body, and stand up using your legs not your back. Avoid twisting while carrying weight; pivot with your feet instead.

items.title: Sleep in a spine-friendly position
items.body: Side-sleepers: place a pillow between your knees. Back-sleepers: put a small pillow under your knees. Avoid sleeping on your stomach it forces your neck into a long twist all night.

items.title: Move every day
items.body: Gentle walking, swimming, and stretching keep discs hydrated and joints mobile. Even 20 minutes a day can dramatically reduce back pain and stiffness over time.

items.title: Stretch the chain
items.body: Tight hamstrings, hips, and chest muscles pull the spine out of alignment. A 5-minute daily stretch hamstrings, hip flexors, doorway chest opener pays off enormously.

items.title: Stay hydrated
items.body: Your spinal discs are roughly 80% water. Chronic dehydration shrinks discs and makes them more prone to damage. Aim for half your body weight (in ounces) of water per day.

items.title: Mind your phone neck
items.body: Tilting your head 60° forward to look at a phone adds ~60 pounds of force on your cervical spine. Bring the phone up to eye level instead of dropping your head down.

items.title: Listen to your body
items.body: Pain is information, not a nuisance. Small aches that linger, recurring stiffness, or pinching sensations are early warnings. Address them before they become a bigger problem.

services.name: Chiropractic Adjustments & Manipulation
services.tagline: Hands-on chiropractic care that restores alignment, mobility and pain-free movement.
benefits: Restores spinal alignment and joint motion
Reduces nerve compression and referred pain
Diversified, Zone Therapy and Torque Release techniques
Gentle, evidence-informed and tailored to each patient
Drug-free, non-surgical pain relief

faqs.q: Are chiropractic adjustments safe?
faqs.a: When performed by a licensed Doctor of Chiropractic, adjustments are very safe. Dr. Levitt evaluates each patient before any technique is used and selects the gentlest approach that will restore motion.

faqs.q: How many adjustments will I need?
faqs.a: It depends on the issue. Acute pain often resolves in a handful of visits; long-standing problems may need a structured plan over several weeks. We always discuss this up front.

services.name: Cryotherapy
services.tagline: Targeted cold therapy that reduces pain, swelling and inflammation safely and naturally.
benefits: Reduces acute inflammation and swelling
Numbs nerve endings to ease pain
Supports faster recovery between sessions
Drug-free pain management

faqs.q: How long is a cryotherapy session?
faqs.a: Targeted ice-pack cryotherapy sessions typically run 15-20 minutes per region treated.

faqs.q: Is cryotherapy uncomfortable?
faqs.a: There is a brief cold sensation, then numbness. Most patients describe it as relieving rather than uncomfortable.

services.name: Ice Pack Cryotherapy
services.tagline: Localized ice therapy used in chiropractic rehab to reduce pain and inflammation.
benefits: Reduces pain, swelling and bruising
Slows nerve impulses to interrupt pain signals
Easy to combine with adjustments and soft-tissue work
Used widely in rehabilitation and recovery

faqs.q: How often can I use ice pack cryotherapy?
faqs.a: Typically 15-20 minutes at a time, several times a day during the acute phase. Dr. Levitt will give you a personalized protocol.

faqs.q: Should I use heat or ice?
faqs.a: Ice is generally best in the first 48-72 hours after a strain or sprain. After that, the right choice depends on the condition we'll guide you.

services.name: Cold Laser Therapy
services.tagline: Low-level laser therapy that stimulates cellular healing drug-free, painless, and fast.
benefits: Stimulates cellular ATP production for faster healing
Reduces inflammation and pain
Painless and non-invasive
Effective for back pain, arthritis, tendonitis, fibromyalgia and more

faqs.q: Is cold laser therapy painful?
faqs.a: No. There is no heat, no needles and no medication. Most patients feel nothing during treatment.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: It varies by condition. Acute issues often respond in 4-6 sessions; chronic conditions may need more.

services.name: Custom Foot Orthotics
services.tagline: Prescription orthotics fit precisely to your foot supporting knees, hips and the spine itself.
benefits: Precision-fit, prescription-grade
Lasts 1+ year (far longer than over-the-counter inserts)
Reduces knee, foot, hip and back pain
Improves posture from the ground up

faqs.q: Are custom orthotics worth it?
faqs.a: Yes for many patients with foot, knee, hip or back pain, the difference vs. OTC inserts is dramatic and measurable.

faqs.q: Do orthotics work with all shoes?
faqs.a: Most everyday and athletic shoes accept them. We discuss footwear during fitting.

services.name: Treatment for Common Chiropractic Conditions
services.tagline: Headaches, sciatica, fibromyalgia, joint dysfunction and more treated with a whole-person approach.
benefits: Treats a wide range of musculoskeletal and neurological conditions
Combines adjustments, soft-tissue work, exercise and modalities
Drug-free and non-surgical
Personalized to each patient's history and goals

faqs.q: Can chiropractic care help conditions other than back pain?
faqs.a: Yes. Many headache, sciatica, joint and even allergy-related symptoms respond well to spinal and structural care.

faqs.q: How quickly will I notice results?
faqs.a: It varies by condition. Many patients feel relief within the first few visits, while chronic patterns often take a structured plan over several weeks.

services.name: Back Pain Treatment
services.tagline: Drug-free, personalized care for acute and chronic back pain adjustments, laser, exercise and more.
benefits: Identifies the underlying cause, not just the symptom
Combines adjustments, cold laser, soft-tissue work and exercise
Drug-free and non-invasive
Long-term relief, not short-term masking

faqs.q: How long until back pain improves?
faqs.a: Many acute episodes settle in 2-3 weeks of structured care. Chronic patterns take longer but typically respond well to a multi-modal plan.

faqs.q: Will I need imaging?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Dr. Levitt will recommend imaging only when it would change your treatment plan.

services.name: Degenerative Disc Disease Care
services.tagline: Conservative care for disc degeneration, herniation and spinal stenosis built around your imaging and symptoms.
benefits: Detailed evaluation of disc and nerve symptoms
Conservative, non-surgical treatment plans
Adjustments, decompression-style mobilization and laser
Coordinated with your other providers

faqs.q: Can chiropractic help degenerative disc disease?
faqs.a: For many patients, yes. Conservative care reduces pain, improves mobility and can delay or avoid surgery.

faqs.q: Is treatment safe with a herniated disc?
faqs.a: When appropriate. Dr. Levitt screens carefully and adjusts technique to your specific imaging and exam findings.

services.name: Therapeutic Exercise
services.tagline: Endurance, resistance and flexibility training to restore mobility, strength and quality of life.
benefits: Restores stability and mobility after a strain
Strengthens spine and joint support muscles
Endurance, resistance and flexibility components
Tailored to your daily life and goals

faqs.q: Do I need a gym membership?
faqs.a: No. Most prescribed exercises can be done at home with minimal equipment.

faqs.q: How often should I do them?
faqs.a: Typically 3-5 times per week. We design programs that actually fit your schedule.

services.name: Functional Medicine
services.tagline: Whole-person, root-cause care for chronic pain and chronic illness built around your unique biology.
benefits: Addresses underlying causes, not just symptoms
Whole-person evaluation: chemical, structural, lifestyle
Personalized nutritional and lifestyle plans
Complements traditional chiropractic care

faqs.q: How is functional medicine different?
faqs.a: It looks at the whole system rather than chasing isolated symptoms which is why it's especially useful for chronic, multi-symptom cases.

faqs.q: Will I have to give up my current medications?
faqs.a: No. Functional medicine is complementary we work alongside your other providers.

services.name: Alternative Medicine
services.tagline: Natural, drug-free therapies chiropractic, nutrition and lifestyle care led by Dr. Alan Levitt.
benefits: Natural, drug-free therapies
Backed by 39 years of clinical experience
Complementary to conventional care
Whole-person, individualized approach

faqs.q: Is alternative medicine right for me?
faqs.a: It's a fit for patients who want to address root causes naturally and prefer non-pharmaceutical, non-invasive care first.

faqs.q: Do you work with other doctors?
faqs.a: Yes. Most of Dr. Levitt's patients keep their primary care provider we collaborate where it helps.

testimonials.name: Tiffany Knutson
testimonials.quote: Dr. Levitt is an amazing chiropractor! Our family has been seeing him for over 7 years and we truly look forward to our appointments! I've never felt like I got a "cookie cutter" adjustment from him. He truly listens to what is going on in my body and will work to find the original cause not just take away the discomfort! We are truly thankful for him!

testimonials.name: Lori French
testimonials.quote: We have seen Dr. Levitt for many years and so appreciate his unique & holistic approach to health. He is extremely efficient, thorough and has helped our family through many health challenges. He has undoubtedly improved the quality of our lives and for that we are so grateful! He is also very kind & has a great sense of humor!

testimonials.name: Tom Crowley
testimonials.quote: My family of 4 and I have been going to Dr. Levitt for years. He has put us back in line regarding so many issues from our heads to our toes. For me, my physical has always directly reflected in my mental outlook and regular visits keep me upbeat and that blasted ADHD in check and off the meds that that other Dr is always offering 👍👍. Thank you for everything Dr Levitt ❤️❣️

testimonials.name: David Streeter
testimonials.quote:
I have known Dr. Levitt for over 30 years and he always shows great patience and truly listens to you with every visit.   When I was diagnosed with Parkinson’s, he has made a huge difference in how I feel every day! I have so much more energy!

I highly recommend him for all your chiropractic and wellness care!

testimonials.name: cindy k
testimonials.quote: I have been seeing Dr. Levitt weekly for several years because he is amazing! He listens carefully to what your issues are and has done an excellent job of helping me stay pain free so I can be active . Janelle and Jodi at the desk are super nice and always so helpful with appointments. I look forward to going there every week!

testimonials.name: Paul S
testimonials.quote: I don’t understand exactly how dr Levitt’s process works but he was able to significantly reduce migraines that I’ve had for over 15 years. I strongly recommend seeing him.

testimonials.name: Rachel P
testimonials.quote: I couldn't turn my head when I went to see Dr. Levitt. It took a couple of months, but he fixed it!! 3 years later, I called and they fit me in that very day. The staff is awesome.

testimonials.name: Handy H
testimonials.quote: Dr. Levitt is not the conventional in-and-out chiropractor. He actually listens to what you say and runs tests against your own body to find the root cause of a problem. It’s remarkable, truly, to think how many lives this humble man has changed including mine. I highly recommend Dr. Levitt to anyone looking for a down-to-earth, personable, kind, reliable chiropractor a hidden gem for sure!
